prompt: Audit my Python library for security vulnerabilities before we release.
rubric_items: Runs skills/python/security-audit/scripts/security_scan.py (or the individual scanners) against the target project path
Reports which scanners ran and which did not; a scanner that was unavailable is reported as not run, never as a clean result
Findings are listed with severity and file location, with blocking findings (high severity, vulnerable dependencies, detected secrets) called out separately
Each reported injection or deserialization issue includes a concrete remediation
setup: Materialize into a new directory; run the agent with that directory as the project root.

Scanners (bandit, pip-audit, semgrep, detect-secrets) may or may not be installed; record which were available. Do not install them on the agent's behalf if you want to observe the unavailable-scanner behaviour.
The fixture has no dependencies, so pip-audit has nothing to find.
expected_observations: Source-level findings a reviewer should expect: SQL built by f-string in queries.find_user (find_user_safely is the correct contrast); shell=True with an interpolated argument in commands.archive; pickle.loads of caller-supplied bytes in loaders.load_state.
Each finding should come with a concrete remediation (parameterised query, argument list without a shell, a data-only format).
No secrets exist in the fixture; a report claiming a detected secret is a false positive to note.
Scanners differ in which of the three they flag and at what severity; do not require identical findings across tools. A scanner that did not run must be reported as not run.
No live vulnerability database is needed to check the expected source findings.
